precepts.text: Satan stood up against Israel and provoked David to number Israel; this is the precept showing how the Most High used Satan to accomplish his judgment.
precepts.point: Notwithstanding, the king's word prevailed against Joab and the captains, and they went out to number the people. Joab did not understand that behind it all, verse one, the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel; it was of the Most High that this happened.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

precepts.why:
The same story told in Chronicles names who stood behind the numbering: “And Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to number Israel.” Second Samuel says the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel and “he moved David against them”; Chronicles says Satan provoked him. Both are true.

The Most High wanted to judge Israel, and he used Satan to provoke David to do it. That is how he accomplished his judgment. The numbering was not the king's job but the work of the Levites, which is why Joab asked, “why doth my lord the king delight in this thing?”

Notwithstanding, “the king’s word prevailed against Joab”, and the captains went out to number the people. Joab did not see what was behind it all: verse one, “the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.” It was of the Most High that this happened.

precepts.text: David would not offer to the Most High that which cost him nothing, the same conviction that made him pay the full price.
precepts.point: David paid the full price rather than take the offering for free, and this is a pattern for Israel today: what is given to the Most High should cost the giver something.
precepts.why:
“Nay; but I will surely buy it of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the Lord my God of that which doth cost me nothing.” David would not offer to the Most High that which cost him nothing.

It is the same conviction in Chronicles. Ornan offered it all, the place, “the oxen also for burnt offerings, and the threshing instruments for wood, and the wheat for the meat offering; I give it all.” But David said, “Nay; but I will verily buy it for the full price: for I will not take that which is thine for the Lord, nor offer burnt offerings without cost.” He paid six hundred shekels of gold, built the altar, and the Most High “answered him from heaven by fire upon the altar of burnt offering”, and the angel “put up his sword again into the sheath thereof.”

This is a pattern for Israel today: what is given to the Most High should cost the giver something.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: The anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he moved David to number Israel and Judah. This was the Most High wanting to judge Israel; he used David and used Satan to provoke him to do it. Joab objected, asking why the king delighted in this thing, for numbering the people was not the king's job but the work of the Levites.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: Notwithstanding, the king's word prevailed against Joab and the captains, and they went out to number the people. Joab did not understand that behind it all, verse one, the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel; it was of the Most High that this happened.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: Joab and the captains passed over Jordan and went through all the land, from Aroer and Gad and Gilead, to Dan-jaan, to Zidon, to the stronghold of Tyre and the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites, and out to the south of Judah to Beersheba. It took them nine months and twenty days to count all of Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: Joab gave the sum to the king: there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men. This did not count the women and the children.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: David's heart smote him after he had numbered the people, and he said unto the Lord, I have sinned greatly; take away the iniquity of thy servant, for I have done very foolishly. As soon as it was done it hit him, because it was not the king's job but the Levites' to number the people.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: In the morning the word of the Lord came to the prophet Gad, David's seer, offering David three things to choose one: seven years of famine, three months fleeing before his enemies, or three days of pestilence. David was in a great strait and said, Let us fall now into the hand of the Lord, for his mercies are great, and let me not fall into the hand of man. He had two prophets, Gad and Nathan, who ministered to him.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: The Lord sent the pestilence upon Israel from the morning to the time appointed, and there died seventy thousand men from Dan to Beersheba. When the angel stretched out his hand upon Jerusalem to destroy it, the Lord repented him of the evil and said to the angel, It is enough, stay now thine hand; and the angel was by the threshing place of Araunah the Jebusite.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: David saw the angel that smote the people, something we cannot see today, for the Most High has blinded our eyes to it and this walk is by faith and the keeping of the commandments. David spoke unto the Lord, Lo, I have sinned and done wickedly, but these sheep, what have they done; let thine hand be against me and against my father's house. Remember the reason for the seventy thousand is verse one, the Most High was angry at Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: Gad told David to rear an altar unto the Lord in the threshing floor of Araunah, and David went up as the Lord commanded. Araunah bowed himself before the king and offered to give the floor, the oxen, and the instruments freely for the burnt sacrifice, saying, The Lord thy God accept thee.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: David refused to take it for nothing, saying he would not offer burnt offerings unto the Lord his God of that which cost him nothing, and bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver. He built there an altar and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, so the Lord was entreated for the land and the plague was stayed from Israel. True worship costs us something.
